ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a conical water tank, with the pointed end below, and the opening above and widening upward. The water surface is at a certain height inside the cone, and on the right a vertical arrow marks the water depth h from the pointed end of the cone upward to the height of the water surface. Reasoning: Water is poured in at a constant volume flow rate, so the volume V of the water is proportional to time t, that is, V = kt. Since the water formed in the cone is also a small cone similar to the whole cone, when the water depth is h, the water-surface radius r is proportional to h. The cone volume V = (1/3)πr^2h, therefore V is proportional to h^3. Since V is proportional to t, h^3 is proportional to t, so h is proportional to t^(1/3). The function t^(1/3) increases with time but its slope gradually decreases, therefore the graph is concave downward. Final answer: concave downward

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the reservoir is a cone with its pointed vertex at the bottom and widening upward, and h is the vertical water depth measured upward from the tip. From the text, water is poured in at a constant volumetric rate, so the water volume V is proportional to time t. Use similarity of cones: at water depth h, the water forms a smaller cone similar to the whole reservoir, so its radius is proportional to h. Therefore V = (1/3)πr^2h is proportional to h^3. Since V = kt, h is proportional to t^(1/3). The graph of t^(1/3) has decreasing slope and is concave downward.

Final answer: concave downward
